sources.publisher: CERT-In, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India
sources.why: Establishes the six-hour reporting obligation and the Annexure I list of reportable incident types. This is the CERT-In clock in the product.

Commercial Banks Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework Directions, 2026. Paragraph 182 carries the six-hour RBI DAKSH reporting obligation from detection. This is the DAKSH clock in the product.

The operative Directions themselves, dated 28.04.2022. Carries the six-hour reporting obligation from noticing and the Annexure I list of reportable incident types. Directions70B.jsp is only a link hub - this is the rule text.
Extension of enforcement timelines. Real regulation is amended in place by later notices; a grounding corpus that ignores amendments is wrong.
Official interpretation of the Directions, including what 'noticing' means for the purpose of starting the clock.
The field list our CERT-In-compatible draft mirrors. Guidance, not a mandatory form - VIGIL must not claim this form is required.
